# Released-schema upgrade fixtures

Schema v1 has no previously released schema. A populated prior-release upgrade fixture is
therefore **N/A for v1 only**, following the VT-03 matrix in
[plan.md](../../../specs/001-ai-task-manager/plan.md). The initial migration, repeat migration,
real-file reopening, native pragmas, storage constraints, indexes and retained history are
covered by [database.test.ts](../../integration/database.test.ts).

These tests require production lock/open/migrate modules and reviewed Drizzle migrations
from T009–T014. Before those exist, execution is **pending**, not a passing test or evidence
of a domain failure. Do not replace production migrations with fixture DDL or mock SQLite,
and do not silently skip the suite when an import or migration is missing.

Starting with the first upgrade after a released schema, commit a small, populated SQLite
fixture generated by that release's production migrations and commands. Include a manifest
with release/schema versions, fixture generator command, SQLite version, SHA-256 checksum,
expected settings/epoch, entity counts and immutable historical rows. Keep fixtures synthetic
and free of private task descriptions or credentials.

Populate projects with distinct priority/workflow models, ordinary/recurring and archived
tasks, dependencies, generations/checkpoints/intervals, all occurrence outcomes, permanent
emoji reservations including absent historical owners, semantic configuration/audit snapshots
and operation receipts. Preserve original fixture bytes: copy it to a temporary directory,
acquire the production lifetime lock, open it and run the production upgrade path there.
Assert current constraints/pragmas/integrity, exact surviving IDs/instants/priority values,
unchanged audit/config/receipt snapshot bytes and marker ownership. Reopen and rerun migrations
to verify durability and idempotence. Add failure/rollback cases for each incompatible or
invalid upgrade input; never regenerate old fixtures through the new schema to make them pass.
